newsitem.title: INDIA: India's former premier Rao faces test in court.
newsitem.headline: India's former premier Rao faces test in court.

text.p: Former Indian prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao faces a crucial week in court and possible arrest as pressure mounts on him to quit as Congress party leader in parliament.
Rao's first major test is on Monday when the Delhi High Court takes up his demand for legal protection against arrest in a forgery case.

The court will take up an anticipatory bail application issued by a lower court which empowered authorities to arrest Rao, who served as prime minister from mid-1991 until last May and opened India to foreign investment and trade.
However Rao's lawyers sought legal protection for him till Monday citing illness, mainly diabetes and hypertension, as reasons for seeking bail.

Lawyers following the case said the Delhi High Court would either grant him anticipatory bail and save him the ignominy of arrest or he would become the first Indian prime minister to be taken into custody facing criminal proceedings.
Even if Rao does get bail, lawyers said his passport would be impounded and he would have to be available at all times for questioning by police.

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) charged Rao and three others on September 26 in the forgery case involving an alleged attempt in 1989 to tarnish the reputation of V.P. Singh, an opposition leader who later became prime minister.

Congress, which has ruled India for all but four years since independence in 1947, took a step towards refurbishing the party's image by inducting former finance minister Manmohan Singh into its top decision-making panel on Sunday.

Singh, a former university professor, was finance miniser in the government of former premier P.V. Narasimha Rao, which lost power in elections this year, launching India into the world's economy by introducing sweeping economic reforms.
Known for his integrity and clean image, Singh's induction into the party's top brass comes as the party is being dogged by corruption charges.
Asked whether Singh would be invited to lead Congress in parliament, a job currently held by Rao, Kesri said:
"Please do not underestimate Manmohan Singh's elevation as it is a very indicative step forward," Congress president Sitaram Kesri said.

Rao quit in disgrace as Congress Party leader last month when a judge upheld a summons ordering him to appear in court to face charges in another case, involving conspiracy to cheat a businessman of $100,000.
Rao has been summoned to appear in court for the cheating case on Wednesday.
The Supreme Court is to take up a police request on Monday that the cheating case be moved to a more secure location.
The police said extremist militants could attack Rao if he appeared in a lower court situated in one of the most congested areas in New Delhi.
